title: Two amounts in a restaurant’s health order match an unrelated construction case

beats.text: A receipt at the Grotto showed a 4% charge for employee health.

visual.sub: A restaurant receipt showed a charge for employee health care

beats.text: A hearing officer found the restaurant had missed its required health payments.

visual.kicker: A restaurant receipt showed a charge for employee health care

beats.text: A payroll subpoena recovered records from 2021 through 2023.

visual.kicker: A payroll subpoena and common ownership changed the headcount

beats.text: Common ownership with other restaurants put the Grotto in the large employer category.

visual.kicker: A payroll subpoena and common ownership changed the headcount

beats.text: The City assessed restitution for 43 workers.

visual.label: The agency listed restitution for 43 workers

beats.text: The signed order gives a total of $181,609.20.

visual.label: Total on the signed restaurant order

beats.text: Its itemized amounts fall short by $32,203.20.
Two of its figures also appear in a separate 2021 construction wage case.
Both amounts match to the cent. The records do not explain why.

visual.kicker: The same two figures appear in an earlier construction case

beats.text: A corrected order or a payment ledger could show what the workers actually received.

visual.kicker: The signed order does not reconcile to its own line items

beats.text: Every source is linked in the case file below.
